title: DocumentationCoverageAndSourceReview
description: Compatibility filename; not a clinical readiness score. It carries two independent things and they must not be conflated: documentation_coverage / projection_coverage (what the archive HAS, and what of it reached a structured slot) and review_flags[] (what a human must look at). Every review flag declares an `audience`: `clinician` flags are the only ones a patient-facing / visit-prep surface may render as 「请医生确认」; `internal_qc` flags are transcription/QC noise that belongs on the internal review surface and must be collapsed to a single line for the family.

projection_coverage.description: How much of what the archive HOLDS actually reached a structured slot. documentation_coverage answers 「does a document exist?」; this answers 「did its content get lifted?」. Without it a best-effort projection is indistinguishable from a complete one: a novel report can be fully transcribed, filed, and still contribute zero structured facts with no signal anywhere. EVERY source_id in source_inventory.json must appear in per_source — including kind=unreadable and kind=novel sources, which are exactly the ones a coverage number would otherwise hide.

source_id.description: Must match a source_id in source_inventory.json.

unprojected_field_classes.description: Classes of field present in this source's transcript that did NOT reach any structured slot, e.g. ["lab_values", "imaging_measurements"]. An EMPTY array means fully projected. Descriptive only — never a statement that the missing content was clinically unimportant.

note.description: Optional short reason, e.g. "no pinned slot for microbiome abundances".

sources_total.description: Count of distinct source_id in source_inventory.json; must equal len(per_source).

sources_fully_projected.description: per_source rows whose unprojected_field_classes is empty.

unreadable_sources.description: inventory rows with kind=unreadable. Never counted as covered anywhere.

category.description: What KIND of problem this is. A closed enum (organize v3) because the free-form string it replaced was never populated by producers, which made downstream filtering impossible and forced visit-prep to render every flag as a clinician action. transcription_disagreement = two read channels disagreed on a character/number. ocr_artifact = a transcription defect with no clinical content (phantom glyphs, rotation, dead scan). untrusted_content_marker = instruction-shaped text found in archive content. pii_semantic_deferred = the semantic PII pass was auditably deferred for a text-only increment and is still owed. source_conflict = two SOURCES state different clinical facts (a real clinician question, not a read error). source_faithfulness = a value could not be reproduced from its cited source span. coverage_gap = material exists but never reached a structured slot (mirrors projection_coverage). The first four are ALWAYS internal_qc.

audience.description: Who this flag is for. REQUIRED — an unlabelled flag used to be rendered to the family as 「请医生确认」 regardless of whether it was a clinical question or an OCR decimal point, so the real ones drowned. clinician = a genuine cross-source clinical question worth a doctor's minute. internal_qc = quality noise the organizing side owns; patient-facing surfaces collapse these into one line and never present them as medical findings. Categories transcription_disagreement / ocr_artifact / untrusted_content_marker / pii_semantic_deferred MUST be internal_qc.

source_ref.description: Where this competing value came from. Three legal forms, because the three situations are genuinely different and collapsing them produced fake anchors. (a) A sidecar ANCHOR (NN_…/….md[#span]) when the value sits in a filed source. (b) `source:<source_id>` when the value is attributable to an inventoried upload but not to a specific filed sidecar span — e.g. a 15_ open source, which is deliberately not anchorable (Q7). (c) null when the value has no source at all: a patient-reported figure, or a field the archive simply disagrees about with nothing to point at. null is an honest record; inventing an anchor to satisfy a required string was the defect.
